'''Jamaree Ray-Shaun Bouyea''' (born June 27, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Phoenix Suns]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[San Francisco Dons men's basketball|San Francisco Dons]].

==High school career==
Bouyea played basketball for [[Palma School]] in [[Salinas, California]]. As a junior, he averaged 18 points and led his team to the Division IV state championship. In his senior season, he averaged 19.1 points and 6.1 assists per game.<ref>{{cite web |last=Gorcey |first=Ryan |title=USF basketball's Jamaree Bouyea returns home for a resounding win over LIU-Brooklyn at Cal State Monterey Bay |url=https://www.sfexaminer.com/sports/usf-basketballs-jamaree-bouyea-returns-home-for-a-resounding-win-over-liu-brooklyn-at-cal-state-monterey-bay/ |website=[[San Francisco Examiner]] |access-date=September 13, 2021 |date=November 19, 2018}}</ref> Bouyea became the first player in 18 seasons to repeat as ''[[The Monterey County Herald|The Monterey Herald]]'' All-County Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite web |last=Devine |first=John |title=The Herald's All-County Boys Basketball Team: Palma guard Jamaree Bouyea leaves winning legacy |url=https://www.montereyherald.com/2017/04/01/the-heralds-all-county-boys-basketball-team-palma-guard-jamaree-bouyea-leaves-winning-legacy/ |website=[[The Monterey County Herald]] |access-date=September 13, 2021 |date=April 1, 2017}}</ref> He was lightly recruited and considered attending [[College-preparatory school|prep school]] for a fifth year.<ref>{{cite web |last=Devine |first=John |title=Palma's Bouyea nets scholarship to USF |url=https://www.montereyherald.com/2017/04/13/palmas-bouyea-nets-scholarship-to-usf/ |website=[[The Monterey County Herald]] |access-date=September 13, 2021 |date=April 13, 2017}}</ref> He accepted an offer from [[San Francisco Dons men's basketball|San Francisco]], the only [[NCAA Division I]] program to offer him a basketball scholarship.<ref>{{cite web |last=Buestad |first=Connor |title="From Seaside to The Hilltop" - Jamaree Bouyea's steady rise to stardom at the University of San Francisco |url=https://section925.com/sports/2021/1/22/from-seaside-to-the-hilltop-jamaree-bouyeas-steady-rise-to-stardom-at-the-university-of-san-francisco |website=Section925 |access-date=September 13, 2021 |date=January 22, 2021}}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman at San Francisco, Bouyea averaged 2.5 points per game, shooting 32.7 percent from the field.<ref>{{cite web |last=Patton |first=Andy |title=WCC Basketball: Breakout candidates from each team for 2019-20 |url=https://bustingbrackets.com/2019/07/18/wcc-basketball-breakout-candidates-team-2019-20/8/ |website=Busting Brackets |access-date=September 13, 2021 |date=July 18, 2019}}</ref> In his sophomore season, he averaged 6.2 points and 3.3 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web |last=Devine |first=John |title=Blistering start on the hardwood for Bouyea |url=https://www.montereyherald.com/2019/11/23/blistering-start-on-the-hardwood-for-bouyea/ |website=[[The Monterey County Herald]] |access-date=September 13, 2021 |date=November 23, 2019}}</ref> He became a regular starter as a junior, averaging 12.2 points, 4.4 rebounds and 3.5 assists per game, and was selected to the All-[[West Coast Conference]] (WCC) Honorable Mention.<ref>{{cite web |last=Devine |first=John |title=Bouyea opens basketball season with a bang for USF |url=https://www.montereyherald.com/2020/12/02/bouyea-opens-basketball-season-with-a-bang-for-usf/ |website=[[The Monterey County Herald]] |access-date=September 13, 2021 |date=December 2, 2020}}</ref> On November 27, 2020, Bouyea led San Francisco to a 61–60 upset win against No. 4 [[2020–21 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]], adding 19 points and six assists.<ref>{{cite web |last=Blackwell |first=Drea |title=Palma basketball star leads San Francisco in upset over No. 4 Virginia |url=https://www.ksbw.com/article/palma-basketball-star-leads-san-francisco-in-upset-over-no-4-virginia/34808292# |website=[[KSBW]] |access-date=September 13, 2021 |date=November 27, 2020}}</ref> On February 18, 2021, he scored a career-high 33 points in a 68–63 loss to [[2020–21 Loyola Marymount Lions men's basketball team|Loyola Marymount]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Devine |first=John |title=Bouyea chasing basketball milestones at USF |url=https://www.montereyherald.com/2021/02/20/bouyea-chasing-milestones-at-usf/ |website=[[The Monterey County Herald]] |access-date=September 13, 2021 |date=February 20, 2021}}</ref> As a senior, Bouyea averaged 17.3 points, 3.7 assists and 3.7 rebounds per game, earning First Team All-WCC honors. He opted to return to college for a fifth season.<ref>{{cite web |last=Mitchell |first=Greg |title=San Francisco has Golden opportunity behind Jamaree Bouyea |url=https://www.midmajormadness.com/2021/9/8/22656214/san-francisco-dons-usf-todd-golden-jamaree-bouyea-khalil-shabazz-wcc-rank-ncaa-basketball-preview |website=Mid-Major Madness |access-date=September 13, 2021 |date=September 8, 2021}}</ref> Bouyea was again named to the First Team All-WCC in 2022.<ref name=WCCAwards>{{cite press release|url=https://wccsports.com/news/2022/3/2/mens-basketball-timme-tabbed-wcc-player-of-the-year.aspx|title=Timme Tabbed WCC Player Of The Year|publisher=[[West Coast Conference]] |date=March 2, 2022 |access-date=March 2, 2022}}</ref> On March 17, 2022, Bouyea scored a career-high 36 points during San Francisco's 92–87 overtime loss to [[2021–22 Murray State Racers men's basketball team|Murray State]] during the opening round of the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NCAA tournament: USF falls to Murray State in OT, despite Bouyea's big night |url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2022/03/17/ncaa-tournament-usf-falls-to-murray-state-in-ot-despite-bouyeas-big-night/ |website=Mercury News |date=18 March 2022 |access-date=18 March 2022}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Sioux Falls Skyforce / Miami Heat / Washington Wizards (2022–2023)===
After going undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]], Bouyea signed with the [[Miami Heat]] on July 14, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|title=HEAT SIGN JAMAREE BOUYEA|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-jamaree-bouyea-071322|website=NBA.com|date=July 14, 2022|access-date=July 17, 2022}}</ref> He was waived on October 13.<ref>{{cite web|title=HEAT CONVERT DRU SMITH TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-convert-dru-smith-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=October 13, 2022|access-date=February 13, 2023}}</ref>

On October 24, 2022, Bouyea joined the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] training camp roster.<ref>{{cite web|title=SKYFORCE ANNOUNCES TRAINING CAMP ROSTER AHEAD OF 2022-23 SEASON|url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-announces-training-camp-roster-ahead-of-2022-23-season/|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2022|access-date=October 24, 2022}}</ref>

On February 7, 2023, Bouyea signed a 10-day contract with the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{cite tweet|first=Shams|last=Charania|title=The Miami Heat are signing guard Jamaree Bouyea to a 10-day contract out of their NBA G League Sioux Falls affiliate, sources tell @TheAthletic @Stadium. Bouyea is averaging 19 points, 5 assists and 5 rebounds for Sioux Falls this season.|number=1623139463755976704|user=ShamsSharania|date=February 7, 2023|access-date=September 28, 2023}}</ref> Bouyea made his NBA debut against the [[Houston Rockets]] on February 10<ref name="RocketsAtHeat">{{cite web|title=Heat top Rockets with last-second alley-oop|url=https://www.nba.com/game/hou-vs-mia-0022200840/box-score|website=NBA.com|date=February 10, 2023|access-date=February 11, 2023}}</ref> and on February 19, he was reacquired by the Skyforce.<ref name="22_23Trans">{{cite web|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/22-23-nba-g-league-transactions|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 19, 2023}}</ref>

On March 3, 2023, Bouyea signed a 10-day contract with the [[Washington Wizards]],<ref>{{cite web|first=Jon|last=Devine|title=NBA: Jamaree Bouyea signs 10-day contract with Wizards|url=https://www.montereyherald.com/2023/03/02/nba-jamaree-bouyea-signs-10-day-contract-with-wizards/|website=MontereyHerald.com|date=March 3, 2023|access-date=March 3, 2023}}</ref> returning to Sioux Falls after the deal expired.<ref name="22_23Trans"/>

On July 1, 2023, Bouyea signed a two-way contract with the [[Miami Heat]],<ref>{{cite web|title=HEAT SIGN JAMAREE BOUYEA TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-jamaree-bouyea-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2023|access-date=July 1, 2023}}</ref> but was waived on September 27.<ref>{{cite web|title=HEAT Make Roster Moves|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-make-roster-moves-20230927|website=NBA.com|date=September 27, 2023|access-date=September 27, 2023}}</ref> On October 30, he returned to the Skyforce.<ref>{{cite web|title=Skyforce Announces Training Camp Roster Ahead of 2023-24 Season|url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-announces-training-camp-roster-ahead-of-2023-24-season|website=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=January 28, 2024}}</ref>

===Portland Trail Blazers (2023)===
On November 12, 2023, Bouyea signed a two-way contract with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Sign Jamaree Bouyea To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-jamaree-bouyea-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=November 12, 2023|access-date=November 12, 2023}}</ref> However, he was waived on November 22.<ref>{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Waive Jamaree Bouyea|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-waive-jamaree-bouyea|website=NBA.com|date=November 22, 2023|access-date=November 23, 2023}}</ref>

===Return to Sioux Falls (2023–2024)===
On November 25, 2023, Bouyea returned to the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Game Preview: vs Wolves|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/game-preview-vs-wolves/n-6034325|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 25, 2023|access-date=November 26, 2023}}</ref>

===San Antonio / Austin Spurs (2024–2025)===
On March 2, 2024, Bouyea signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[San Antonio Spurs]],<ref>{{cite tweet|first=Tom|last=Orsborn|title=#Spurs make the following moves reported earlier official: 1, They've converted Barlow's two-way deal to a standard NBA contract; 2, They've signed RaiQuan Gray and Jamaree Bouyea to two-way deals; 3, They've waived forward Mamadi Diakite.|number=1764032846534959265|user=tom_orsborn|date=March 2, 2024|access-date=March 2, 2024}}</ref> but on September 15, he was waived by the Spurs.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Austin Spurs|title=The San Antonio Spurs today announced that they have waived Two-Way guard Jamaree Bouyea.|number=1835407348476555728|user=austin_spurs|date=September 15, 2024|access-date=September 15, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Stinar|title=San Antonio Spurs Reportedly Release 2-Year NBA Player|url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/san-antonio-spurs-reportedly-release-2-year-nba-player-bouyea|website=SI.com|date=September 15, 2024|access-date=September 15, 2024}}</ref> However, he was re-signed on October 18<ref>{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Spurs Sign Jamaree Bouyea To Exhibit 10 Deal|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/10/spurs-sign-jamaree-bouyea-to-exhibit-10-deal.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 18, 2024|access-date=October 19, 2024}}</ref> and waived the next day.<ref>{{cite web|first=Arthur|last=Hill|title=Spurs Waive Malachi Flynn, Brandon Boston|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/10/spurs-waive-malachi-flynn-brandon-boston.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 19, 2024}}</ref> On October 29, he rejoined Austin.<ref>{{cite web|title=Austin Spurs Announce 2024 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/austin-spurs-announce-2024-training-camp-roster/n-6160743|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 29, 2024|access-date=November 3, 2024}}</ref>

===Milwaukee Bucks (2025)===
On March 4, 2025, the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] announced that they had signed Bouyea to a [[two-way contract]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Jamaree Bouyea to a Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-jamaree-bouyea-to-a-two-way-contract|date=March 4, 2025|website=NBA|access-date=March 4, 2025}}</ref> He made five appearances (one start) for Milwaukee, averaging 3.4 points, 1.0 rebound, and 2.0 assists.

===Return to Austin Spurs (2025)===
For the [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–26 season]], Bouyea was re-signed by the Austin Spurs.

===Phoenix / Valley Suns (2025–present)===
On November 17, 2025, Bouyea signed with the [[Phoenix Suns]] on a two-way contract.<ref>{{cite web | last=Zimmerman | first=Kevin | title=Suns to sign Jamaree Bouyea on 2-way contract | website=Arizona Sports | date=2025-11-17 | url=https://arizonasports.com/nba/phoenix-suns/sign-jamaree-bouyea/3602675/ | access-date=2025-12-07}}</ref> On March 2, 2026, Bouyea signed a two-year, standard contract with Phoenix.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Suns G Jamaree Bouyea converted to standard contract|url=https://arizonasports.com/nba/phoenix-suns/jamaree-bouyea/3613085/|access-date=March 7, 2026|website=arizonasports.com|language=en}}</ref> On April 12, Bouyea recorded a career-high 27 points with nine assists, five rebounds, two blocks, and one steal in a 135–103 victory over the [[2025–26 Oklahoma City Thunder season|Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Suns' Jamaree Bouyea: Paces Phoenix in win|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/suns-jamaree-bouyea-paces-phoenix-in-win/|access-date=April 25, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}}</ref> He made 46 appearances (including one start) for Phoenix during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], recording averages of 5.7 points, 1.8 rebounds, and 1.8 assists.
